uncertainty.evidence: Current Langfuse v4 interfaces and the existing provider seams needed targeted documentation and code inspection.

scope.evidence: Settings, dependency lock, application construction, five provider operations, lifecycle, tests, and setup documentation are connected.

reasoning.evidence: The boundary must exclude document content, identifiers, credentials, and arbitrary exception text while telemetry failures remain non-blocking.

verification.evidence: Offline tests can prove allowlisting and fail-open behavior; live trace inspection needs user-provided project credentials.

route.ownership: One worker owned the observability adapter, configuration, dependency lock, tests, and documentation; coordinator inspected the privacy boundary and reran checks.

outcome.behavior: Optional manual Langfuse observations wrap OCR, extraction, embeddings, query rewrite, and answers. Export is disabled by default and only activates with an explicit enable flag, complete server-side credentials, and a base URL. Inputs, outputs, identifiers, arbitrary errors, and credentials are excluded by a fixed metadata allowlist. Telemetry initialization/export/shutdown failures fail open.
outcome.privacy_review: Coordinator required closing error observations without passing a provider exception or traceback to the Langfuse context manager; a secret-bearing exception regression test proves this boundary.

verification.tests: Focused observability, foundation, question, and extraction suites passed using the local backend virtual environment with an explicit application path after uv's editable-install synchronization issue.
verification.static: Ruff check, Ruff format check, and mypy passed for observability/configuration/application files.
verification.runtime: Refreshed local backend health endpoint and frontend each returned HTTP 200.
verification.live_langfuse: Not attempted: no Langfuse credentials were supplied, so no external trace or dashboard audit is claimed.
